headline_marked: 7 remanded over [[extremist network disguised as martial arts group]] in Dhaka
headline: 7 remanded over extremist network disguised as martial arts group in Dhaka
summary: Police allege the group used a martial arts cover to recruit followers and spread extremist views to endanger national sovereignty.
details: A Dhaka court has placed seven suspects on a three-day remand for their alleged involvement in an extremist network operating under the guise of martial arts training.
The group, identified as 'Fatah Combat System' or 'Sabir Bhaiyer Jamaat', was allegedly led by martial arts instructor Shah Amanat Sabir.
Police claim the group used Facebook, Messenger, WhatsApp, and Telegram to recruit members and spread extremist views while pretending to offer combat training.
Investigators allege the network aimed to obstruct development activities, endanger Bangladesh's sovereignty, and establish 'Shariah ideology' through militancy.
The suspects were initially detained on July 5 from a field in the Jatrabari area of Dhaka, where police believe they had gathered for extremist training.
Police also cited a video allegedly showing the leader, Sabir, detonating a crude explosive, which he reportedly admitted was recorded to create panic.
Following the arrests, police claim associates of the group posted threatening and provocative messages on Facebook demanding the release of the detainees.
caption:
Martial arts training as a front for extremism? 7 suspects are in remand after police uncovered a hidden network in Dhaka.

A Dhaka court has placed seven suspects on a three-day remand for their alleged involvement in an extremist network operating under the guise of martial arts training.

The group, identified as 'Fatah Combat System' or 'Sabir Bhaiyer Jamaat', was allegedly led by martial arts instructor Shah Amanat Sabir.

Police claim the group used Facebook, Messenger, WhatsApp, and Telegram to recruit members and spread extremist views while pretending to offer combat training.

Investigators allege the network aimed to obstruct development activities, endanger Bangladesh's sovereignty, and establish 'Shariah ideology' through militancy.

The suspects were initially detained on July 5 from a field in the Jatrabari area of Dhaka, where police believe they had gathered for extremist training.

Police also cited a video allegedly showing the leader, Sabir, detonating a crude explosive, which he reportedly admitted was recorded to create panic.

Following the arrests, police claim associates of the group posted threatening and provocative messages on Facebook demanding the release of the detainees.

headline_marked: Tk 982 crore spent on [[Mujib Borsho programmes]] in Bangladesh
headline: Tk 982 crore spent on Mujib Borsho programmes in Bangladesh
summary: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury revealed the expenditure in parliament, detailing costs for statues, memorials, and digital boards.
details: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury informed parliament that a total of Tk 982 crore, 91 lakh and 74 thousand was spent by various ministries and divisions on 'Mujib Borsho' celebrations.

The expenditure covered the construction of images and memorials of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the installation of bronze, copper, and marble statues at government offices, and digital timekeeping boards.
The celebrations, marking the birth centenary of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, were initially scheduled for 2020-21 but were extended by nine months due to the pandemic.
Out of 62 ministries and divisions, 43 incurred expenses. The Local Government Ministry spent the most at Tk 283.15 crore, followed by the Railways Ministry at Tk 206.73 crore.
Other significant spending was recorded by the Cabinet Division (Tk 140.45 crore), Housing and Public Works Ministry (Tk 133.30 crore), and the Home Ministry (Tk 47.66 crore).
Responding to a question from Jamaat MP Mahbubur Rahman Belal, the Finance Minister stated that no decision has yet been taken to audit or investigate the spending.
The minister also noted that the former prime minister's food expenses alone amounted to Tk 35 crore in a single year, as part of a broader verification of previous administration expenditures.
caption:
Nearly Tk 1,000 crore spent on 'Mujib Borsho' celebrations. 

Who spent the most?

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury informed parliament that a total of Tk 982 crore, 91 lakh and 74 thousand was spent by various ministries and divisions on 'Mujib Borsho' celebrations.

The expenditure covered the construction of images and memorials of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the installation of bronze, copper, and marble statues at government offices, and digital timekeeping boards.

The celebrations, marking the birth centenary of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, were initially scheduled for 2020-21 but were extended by nine months due to the pandemic.

Out of 62 ministries and divisions, 43 incurred expenses. The Local Government Ministry spent the most at Tk 283.15 crore, followed by the Railways Ministry at Tk 206.73 crore.

Other significant spending was recorded by the Cabinet Division (Tk 140.45 crore), Housing and Public Works Ministry (Tk 133.30 crore), and the Home Ministry (Tk 47.66 crore).

Responding to a question from Jamaat MP Mahbubur Rahman Belal, the Finance Minister stated that no decision has yet been taken to audit or investigate the spending.

The minister also noted that the former prime minister's food expenses alone amounted to Tk 35 crore in a single year, as part of a broader verification of previous administration expenditures.
